scope: Offline vendor host binaries and existing local manual text only; no device I/O, Windows execution, recovery writer, firmware replacement or Git action.

clear_app.actual_send: RVA 0xc24f calls common RVA 0xc7d0; same runtime selector1/operation2 path as SetGCM; c7d0 uses bound protocol virtual +0x2c
clear_app.qualification: Index is passed through common symbol/address resolution because normalflag=0; not a newly established literal wire request. No evidence that ClearApp is serviced independently when runtime bulk path does not reply.
clear_app.autoshop_call: AutoShop RVA 0x11ffd0b pushes commandLevel0/executeMode1; RVA 0x11ffd0f calls IAT0x1eb0eb4 after connection/permission/UI checks. Not an autonomous boot path.

simple_command.enum_branch0: RVA0x30521..0x30536 writes DWORD1 to local index0xff000010 through common c7d0, normalflag1
simple_command.nonzero_enum_branch: RVA0x3053f..0x30572 reads same index with common c6c0 and copies returned DWORD
simple_command.autoshop_calls: AutoShop RVA0xa7324d passes enum0 once, then RVA0xa7331d polls enum0x7b bounded200; numeric enum0x7b selects the generic nonzero/read branch, not reset123.
simple_command.cross_evidence: Research14 simulator_followup names ff000010 read_load_down_file_status/write_load_down_file_control; simulator names are corroboration only, not physical protocol compatibility.
simple_command.conclusion: Download-file control/status helper over runtime protocol, not a proven CPUReset/recovery endpoint.

control_command.bound_protocol: same protocol virtual+0x2c, selector1/op2, indexff008000/length4 + caller command DWORD
control_command.qualification: No independent channel or reset enum established; not implemented or sent.
